t: Organization of the Imperial Household Ministry of Korea published.
In honor of Mr. Lumieux, Canadian Minister of Labor, the Municipality and business men give a reception at the Peers' Club.
Prince Pu-Lin, Chinese Special Envoy, arrives in Tokyo; leaving on the 13th inst for home.
Launching of the Chiyo-Maru at the Mitsubishi yard.
Arrival of Chaimyon, Korean Envoy, at Tokyo.
Appointment of Viscount Yasushi Nomura as the Chief Guardian of Princesses Fumi and Yasu.
Death of Mr. Chu Asai, an artist.
Launching of the torpedo destroyer Uranami at Maidzuru yard.
The Emperor visits the Korean Prince at the Shiba Detached Palace.
The 24th session of the Imperial Diet convend.
The Korean Envoy leaves Tokyo.
Mr. Lumieux leaves Tokyo for home.
The Emperor personally inspects the cruiser Tsukuba at Yokosuka.
The Emperor honors the opening ceremony of the Diet with his presence.
Prince Fushimi, jr. leaves Shimbashi for Europe.
Viscount Aoki, Ambassador to the U. S. A., is relieved of his post. Baron Takahira, Ambassador to Itaty, is transferred to America.
Return of Mr. Tsuzuki, Special Ambassador at the Hague Peace Conference, to Tokyo.
Death of Gaho Hashimoto, the famous artist of Japanese school.
Baron Sakatani and Mr. Yamagata are relieved of their ministerial chairs.
Mr. Matsuda, Minister of Justice, and Mr. Hara Home Minister, are respectively appointed as additional post to the chairs of Finance and Communications.
The mass meeting of the Seiyukai.
Dr. Hatoyama leaves the Progressives and joins the Seiyukai.
The mass meeting of the Progressves.
Introduction of the Increased Taxation Bill to the Lower House. The mass meeting in Tokyo of all the chambers of commerce throughout the empire.
Mr. Yi Taiyon, Minister of the Korean Imperial Household, returns home.
The joint mass meeting of business men throughout the Empire and demonstration against the Increased Taxation.
The Japanese S.S. Tatsumaru is sized by a Chinese warship off the port of Amoy.
Viscount Aoki is appointed Privy Councillor.
Prince Ito commemorates the 20th anniversary of the promulgation of the constitution at his new residence.
The Budget passes the House of Representatives.
A big fire in Asakusa Park: more than 200 houses destroyed.
The House of Peers adopts the Increased Taxation Bill.
A great fire at Noda, Shimosa province: over 400 houses destroyed.
Dr. Baeltz arrives in Japan.
Baron Naoyuki Ando dies.
Fire at Niigata, over 1,500 houses destroyed.
Commemoration of the Anglo-Japanese alliance at the official residence of the Minister of Foreign Affairs.
Death of Admiral Masanojo Kamimura.
The Tatsu Maru affairs settled.
Laws concerning the increased taxation promulgated.
Mr. Bean, Governor-General of Indo-China, is received in audience by the Emperor.
Mayors and headmen of towns and villages officially rewarded in connetion with the Russo-Japanese War.
The 20th anniversary of the promulgation of the Constitution celebrated by members of Both Houses.
Mr. Stevens, Adviser to the Korean Court, shot at San Francisco by a Korean fanatic.
Appointment of Baron Senge as Minister of Justice, and of Viscount Hotta as Minister of Communications.
Launching of the Mogami at the Nagasaki yard.
Death of Baron Yanosuke Iwasaki and Mr. Stevens.
The closing ceremony of the Imperial Diet.
Prince Ito returns to his post at Seoul.
Prince Arisugawa, jr., dies at Yedajima.
The Crown Prince proceeds to Yamaguchi and Tokushima prefectures.
Snow continues to fall from previous night reaching 6 or 7 inches deep at Tokyo.
Death of Count Matsuura.
Return of the Crown Prince to Tokyo.
Nuptials of Prince Takeda and Princess Tsune solemnited. Sinking of the cruiser Matsushima at the Pescadores owing to the explosion of magazine.
The Japanese Legation at St. Petersburg promoted to Embassy, and Baron Motono to the Ambassador.
Prince Yamashina dies.
A fire at Naoyetsu, over 700 houses burnt down.
The Emperor grants a donation of Y. 30,000 to the Waseda University.
Signing of the American-Japanese arbitration agreement
Mr. Kohei Sufu, Gov. of Kanagawa, is created a Baron.
General election of the members of the Lower House.
Death of Marquis Toku-gawa, formerly Lord of Nagoya.
The Emperor visits the Military Accountants School.
The Empress is present at the general meeting of the Ladies' Patriotic Association held at Aoyama.
Death of Mr. Iwai, Chief of the Formosan Administration Bureau.
The Emperor proceeds to the Military Cadets' School. General Nogi ordered to Manchuria.
Celebration of the 4th Anniversary of the Japan Sea Battle.
The Crown Prince honors the occasion with his presence.
The Emperor proceeds to the Military Preparatory School.
The joint mass meeting of the Tokyo Lawyers' Association; Dr. T. Okamura elected President of the Association.
The 16th general meeting of the Japan Red Cross Society at Hibiya park, the Empress is presented on the occasion.
The joint mass meeting of Agriculture and Industrial Banks.
The Emperor grants a donation of 300,000 yen to the Military and Naval Club.
The Empress proceeds to the Girls' Higher Normal School.

Appointment of Baron Chinda as Ambassador to Germany, Baron G. Hayashi as Ambassador to Italy, Mr. H. Ijuin as Minister to China, Mr. Ishii as Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs, and other changes in the Foreign Office.
Launching of the Volunteer Sakura-Maru at Nagasaki.
Hail-storm at Tokyo in the afternoon.
The joint mass meeting of the chambers of commerce throughout the country.
Unveiling of the monument for Russian Officers and men killed at Port Arthur.
Arrival of Drs. Koch and Sieman.
The opening ceremony of the Disabled Soldiers Home.
Suicide of Bizan Kawakami, the novelist.
Mr. Sakuya Yoshida appointed Minister to Siam.
Death of Doppo Kunikida, the novelist.
Dr. Koch received in audience by the Emperor.
Mr. Loudon, Dutch Minister, presents to the Emperor the letter relieving him of his post.
Big fire at Niitsu, Niigata Prefecture, 450 houses destroyed.
Death of Mr. Iken Kojima.
Municipalization of the Tokyo Electric Rly. rejected by the Government.
Resignation of the Saionji Cabinet. Mr. Hidaka, Chamberlain to His Majesty, despatched to Seoul to ask Prince Ito about the Cabinet change.
The Empress proceeds to the Deaf and Dumb School.
Mr. Baukmeteff, Russian Minister, presents His Majesty with the letter relieving of his post. His successor Mr. Malevitch, Ambassador, arrives in Tokyo.
Graduation ceremony of the Tokyo Imperial University; honored with the Emperor's presence.
Mr. Hidaka, Chamberlain, returns from Seoul.
The Emperor calls Marquis Katsura and summons the elder statesmen.
Commencement ceremony of the Kyoto Imperial University; Prince Higashi-Fushimi is present.
The Katsura Cabinet organized.
Mayor Ozaki tenders his resignation.
The Miye-Maru is transported to Nikolaiesk.
Mr. Malevitch, new Russian Ambassador, received in audience by the Emperor.
Appointment of Mr. N. Oshikawa as Vice-Minister of Agr. & Com.; and of Mr. Wakatsuki as Vice-Minister of Finance.
Dr. K. Ichiki appointed Vice-Minister of Home-Affairs; Mr. E. Kamei, Inspector-General of Metropolitan-Police; and Mr. Arimatsu, Director of the Police Affairs Bureau.
Mr. Sawayanagi, Vice-Minister of Education, resigns, and Mr. Okada succeeds him.
Prince Ito arrives in Tokyo and proceeds to the Imperial Palace. Mr. Tsuzuki resigns his post as Chief Secretary of the Privy Council, and Mr. Kingoro Kawamura suceeds him.
General Prince Fushimi returns to Tokyo.
Count Komura, Ambassador at London, is recalled and leaves London with Mr. Wakatsuki.
Concerning the Miye-Maru, affairs, Consul Nomura lays a protest with the Russian Governor-General.
Exchange of ratifications of the Consular Convention between Japan and Holland.
Mr. Hu Weite, new Chinese Minister, arrives in Tokyo.
Return of the Training Squadron.
Mr. Tsuzuki is created a Baron.
Exchange of ratifications of the Trade-Mark convention between Japan and America.
Promotion of Lieut.Generals H. Inouye and H. Okubo to full Generals, and of Vice-Admiral S. Hidaka to full Admiral.
Publication of the American Japanese Agreement on the right of Industrial and Literary works in China and Korea.
Mr. Murakami, chief of the Naval Paymaster's Bureau, resigns, and Mr. Fukunaga succeeds him.
Captain and men of the Miye-maru are discharged.
Death of Mr. Taizo Miyoshi, ex-president of Supreme Court.
Mr. Kei Hara starts on a tour in Europe and America
Return of Count Komura to Tokyo.
Count Komura appointed Minister of Foreign Affairs.
Regulations of the Oriental Colonization Bank published.
The Katsura Cabinet publishes its opinions on the readjustment of the state finance.
Postponement of the Grand Exhibition of Japan published.
Issue of the Imperial Rescript on the postponement of the Grand Exhibition of Japan.
Baron Dairoku Kikuchi appointed President of the Imperial Kyoto University.
Viscount Kaneko, President of the Grand Exhibition of Japan, relieved of the post at his request.
Sheng Ihui, Chinese Commissioner, arrives in Tokyo.
The Japan China forestry agreement signed.
The America-Japanese arbitration treaty published.
Mr. T. Kato appointed Ambassador to England.
Arrival of Mr. Li Yongku, President of the Il Chin Hoi, in Tokyo.
Baron Hayashi, Ambassador to Rome, leaves Shimbashi for his post.
Baron Chinda, Ambassador to Germany, leaves Shimbashi.
The Governor-General of Kiao-chau Bay arrives in Tokyo.
Mr. Ozaki, Mayor of Tokyo, re-appointed.
Mr. Hioki appointed Minister to Chile.
Mr. Loomis, Chief American Commissioner for the Grand Exhibition, arrives in Japan.
Marshal Marquis Nozu granted Grant Order and Grant Cordon of Rising Sun and Paulownia.
Marquis Kuroda re-elected Vice-President of the House of Peers.
Sale of pari mutuel prohibited.
Viscount Sone resigns his post as Director of the Horse Administration Bureau, and Viscount Terauchi, Minister of War, succeeds.
The Nanki Bunko (library) opens.
Arrival of Tang Shaoi in Tokyo.
Arrival of Amersican businessmen, Mr. Dolman and 56 others, by the Tenyo-Maru.
Imperial Rescript against tendency to extravagance, luxury and speculation promulgated.
Arrival of the American Fleet at Yokohama.
Death of Marshal Marquis Nozu.
Admiral Sperry, U. S. A. Navy, comes up to Tokyo.
Admiral Sperry is received in audience by the Emperor.
Reception of the officers and men of the American Fleet by the Tokyo municipality at Hibiya Park.
Admiral Sperry leaves Tokyo.
Celebration at Taipeh of completion of trunk railway in Formosa.
Baron Sakatani returns from abroad.
The American Fleet leaves Japan.
Death of Admiral Viscount Enomoto.
Sheng Ihui leaves Tokyo.
Arrival of Marquis Guiccioli, Italian Ambassador, in Tokyo.
Return of Lieut.-Gen. Okazaki of the 13th Division, from Korea. Mr. Loomis leaves for home.
Marriage of Prince Miyeko Arisugawa with the son and heir of Prince Keiki Tokugawa.
The Emperor leaves Tokyo to attend the Grand Military Manœuvers at the Kwansai districts.
The Crown Prince personally inspects the Sakura-Maru.
Arrival of Dr. Sven Hedin in Japan.
Close of the Grand Military Manœuvers.
Death of Princess Kwacho.
The Chino-Japanese Railway Convention concluded. The question of the Kirin-Changchun and Hsinmintun-Mukden lines settled.
The Emperor returns to Tokyo.
The 25th anniversary of the establishment of the German Association School. The director and others decorated by the German Emperor.
Marquis Guiccioli, Italian Ambassader, proceeds to the Imperial Palace and presents credentials.
Mr. Manjiro Inagaki, Minister to Spain, dies at his post.
Dr. Hedin leaves Tokyo.
First meeting of the British Association at the Imperial Hotel; Sir Claude McDonald elected President.
Loss of the Denzu-in temple by fire.
Organization of the Railway Board and appointment of its President and other officials published.
Creation of the Reserve Squadrons and Rear-Admirals Nomoto, Yatsushiro, Ide and Takagi appointed Commanders respectively at Kure, Yokosuka, Saseho and Maidzuru
Marchioness Nabeshima, Director of the Ladies Patriotic Association, and others rewarded in connection with the Russo-Japanese war.
Mr. Shinji Tsuji created a Baron.
25th anniversary of the establishment of the Teikoku Kyoiku-kai (Imperial Education Association) celebrated.
Death of General Okazawa Chief Aide-de-Camp to his Mejesty.
Publication of the Mexican-Japanese treaty.
Ambassader Kato leaves Shimbashi for England.
Death of General Baron Hikaru Inouye at Kyoto.
Appointment of Mr. Zeko Nakamura as President, and Mr. Shimbei Kunisawa as Vice-President, of the South Manchuria Railway Co.
Great change among Generals and Divisional Commanders.
Death of Mr. Shuntei Toyabe, editor of the Magazine “Sun.”
25th session of the Imperial Diet begins sitting. Messrs. Haseba and Koedzuka elected President and Vice-President respectively.
Great fire at Ashio: over 100 houses destroyed.
Appointment of Lieut.-General Usagawa to the presidency, and Mr. Yoshiwara to the Vice Presidency, of the Oriental Develepment Co.
Jan Helman van Coyman, proceeds to the Imperial Court and presents his credentials to His Majesty.
Agitation of Tokyo citizens against the increasing of the tramway fare.
Death of Mr. Kotaro Noritake, editor of the “Tokyo Keizai Zasshi.”
Mr. Adamoez, Austrian Ambassador, proceeds to the Imperial Palace to present the letter relieving him of the post.
Korean Emperor leaves on an inspection tour through southern Korea.
The Hokkaido Prefectural Office at Sapporo destroyed by fire.
Princess Nashimoto leaves Yokohama by the S. S. Kamo-maru for Europe.
Korean Emperor returns from his tour.
Appointment of Lieut.-General S. Nakamura as Chief Aide-de-Camp to His Majesty; and of Lieut.-General K. Uchiyama as Commander of the 15th Division.
The Education Minister issues an instruction about moral education.
Application for the increased fare of the Tokyo Tramway Co. rejected.
Death of Viscount Y. Nomura, Privy Councillor.
General Hasegawa returns from Korea.
Arrival at Tokyo of Narasaraja Wadiyao, younger brother of the King of Mysore, India.
Death of Viscount F. Tanaka, Privy Councillor.
Return of the Korean Emperor from his tour in Northern Korea.
Marquis Hachisuka, Count Kabayama and Kagawa appointed Court Councillors.
10th anniversary of the promulgation of the Constitution celebrated at the promotion of the Tokyo Muncipality.
Commemoration of the Anglo-Japanese Alliance at the residence of Count Komura.
Death of Viscount Dr. T. Hashimoto.
The Prince of Mysore leaves Tokyo for home.
53rd general meeting of the Bank of Japan.
Inauguration of the Japanese legation in Chile.
Return of Mr. K. Hara from abroad.
Arrival of Korean Envoy Min. Pyong-hyok and Court ladies in Tokyo.
Viscount Ogyu and Baron Tsuzuki appointed Privy Councillors.
The Progressives expel, Mr. Inukai.
Death of Privy Councillor Baron Honda.
Appointment of Vice-Admiral Arima as Commander of the Saseho Naval Station: and of Vice-Admiral Uryu as member of the Admirals' Council.
Opening of the Japanese Consulate in Batavia.
The Japanese Consulate at Odessa is closed.
The demonstration of weavers at the Kinki-kan.
The Japanese Consulate at Moscow is opened.
Princess Takeda delivered of a Prince.
Baron Culmberg, new Austrian Ambassador, arrives in Tokyo.
Departure of the training ships Aso and Soya from Yokohama for America.
General Kuroki is put on the retired list.
A heavy snow-fall at Tokyo.
Austria Ambassador Baron Culmberg presents his Credentials to His Majesty.
Bankruptcy of Fujimoto bill broker at Osaka.
Princess Kuni leaves for Europe.
Closing ceremony of the 25 session of the Diet.
Arrival of Mr. William Skinner, deligate of American Silk Industry Guild.
50th anniversary of the death of Ii Kamon-no-kami celebrated.
Baron Senge elected President of the Tokyo Street Rly. Co.
The Zōjōji temple destroyed by fire.
Russo-Japanese Convention on the Railway and Steamship through service signed.
Annual meeting of the Ladies' Patriotic Association at Hibiya park.
Dr. Manes, German scholar of insurance, arrives in Tokyo.
The joint meeting of the bankers' clearing houses.
Explosion at a rifle shop, Imahashi, Osaka.
Messrs. Isomura and Akiyama, Director of the Japan Sugar Refinery Co., arrested.
Demise of Rev. Shaku Unsho.
Death of Koki Namma.
Reception of Mr. Skinner at the Tokyo Chamber of Commerce.
A number of M.P.'s. arrested in connection with the Sugar Co. scandal.
Viscount Hotta expelled from the Kenkyu-kai party of Peers' House.
Departure of Prince Fushimi to represent His Majesty at the Imperial Obsequies of China.
Completion of the torpedo-destroyer Isonami at Maizuru.
Arrival of the Korean tourist party, 94 in all, in Tokyo.
Opening ceremony of the Miike Harbor, Chikugo province.
The Imperial banquet of cherry-viewing at the Shiba Detached Palace: T. I. M. the Emperor and Empress present.
Marriage of Prince Kitashirakawa and Princes Kane; Count Sasaki promoted to Marquis.
Arrival of British Chinese Squadron in Yokohama.
Vice-Admiral Lampton, Commanding British Chinese Squadron, arrives in Tokyo.
Marquis Inouye gives a garden party in congratulation of his recovery.
The Bank of Japan lowers interest.
Promulgation of the new newspaper regulations.
The 3rd Squadron of the American Pacific Fleet enters Yokohama.
Part of class room of the Higher Commercial School destroyed by fire.
20 M.P.'s. in connection with the Sugar Co. scandal, proved guilty at the preliminary examination.
Death of Futabatei Hasegawa, novelist.
The city of Kobe loan successfully floated.
Generals Hasegawa, Nishi and Kawamura appointed special Military Inspectors.
Eruption of Mt. Tarumaye, Hokkaido,
Arrival of Rear-Admiral Harper, commanding the American Squadron, in Tokyo.
Graduation ceremony of the Naval college in the presence of the Emperor.
Prince Fushimi returns to Tokyo from China.
The loan of the Keihin Electric Co. concluded.
Mr. James Smith, Governor-General of the Philippines, arrives in Tokyo.
Mr. Chirol, foreign editor of the Times, & Mr. Morrison, Peking Correspondent arrived in Tokyo.
Arrival of Mr. Fairbanks, ex-U. S. Vice-President, and Mrs. Fairbanks in Tokyo.
A big fire at Yokosuka.
The teaching of the Tokyo Higher Commercial School resumed.
The first public trial of the accused in connection with the Japan Sugar Co. scandal.
Mr. Fairbanks received in audience by the Emperor.
Unveiling of the statues of Admirals Saigo, Kawamura and Nire in the compound of the Naval Department.
The first general meeting of the International journalists association at the Imperial Hotel.
Messrs. Chirol and Morrison received in audience by the Emperor.
Prince Fushimi appointed honorary President of the Anglo-Japanese Exhibition.
Messrs. Chirol and Morrison leave for Korea.
General meeting of the Japan Sugar Refinery Co.
Death of Marquis Norimasa Ikeda, formerly Lord of Okayama.
Inauguration of the Kokugi-kan (National Sporting Hall).
Death of Viscount T. Kikkawa, formerly Lord of Iwakuni.
An accident in the Body Guard Engineer battalion at Akabane; many casualties, including Major Sasaki, commanding.
Viscount Sone appointed Resident-General in succession to Prince Ito; and the latter made President of the Privy Council.
Count Tanaka, Minister of Imperial Household, relieved of his office; and Prince Iwakura appointed his successor.
Viscount Sone leaves for his post.
Re-election of officers of the Teikoku Gakushi Kai-in; Baron Kikuchi elected President.
Unveiling of the statue of the late Dr. Hashimoto in the premises of the Red Cross Hospital.
Recognition of merits of the Army stationed in Korea published.
Death of Count Shimadzu, ex-Lord of Sadowara.
Arrival of Russian students' tourist party in Tokyo.
Princess Kan-in delivered of a girl.
50th anniversary of the opening of Yokohama.
Prince Hsai Chong, Chinese Envoy, arrives in Tokyo.
Prince Ito leaves for Korea.
Prince Hsai Cheng received in audience by the Emperor.
The Supreme Court passes final judgment on the accused in connection with the Sugar Co. scandal.
Mr. Zumoto leaves for America.
Viscount Hotta publishes a declaration.
Prince Hsai, Chinese envoy, leaves Tokyo.
Baron de Marchi, new Argentine Minister, arrives at Yokohama.
The Emperor honours the graduation ceremony of the Tokyo Imperial University with his presence.
Finding of the preliminary examination as to the directors of the Japan Sugar Co. scandal published. Dr. Sako, ex-president, commits suicide.
The Emperor proceeds to the graduation ceremony of the Peers' School.
The Fuji Cotton Spinning Factory adopts a resolution increasing its capital to 8,000,000 yen.
South American-Japanese Association and Asiatic Fine-Arts Investigation Association organized.
Return of Prince Ito to Oiso.
Prince Ito received in audience by the Emperor.
The China exploitation company organized.
Lieut.-Gen. (ret.) Yenya, President of the Japan Marine Products Co., convicted at the preliminary examination and deprived of his title and rank.
Death of Eiko Satake, artist.
Publication of the memorandum of the Japan-Korea convention.
Creation of electric and post saving bureaux in the Dept. of communications
Prince Ito appointed the President of the Korean Crown Prince's Education Board.
Provisions of the Central Bank of Korea published.
By-elections of M.P.'s. in several prefectures.
Prince and Princess Nashimoto return from Europe.
The Commercial and Industrial Bureau in the Dept. of Commerce and Agriculture, divided into two Bureaux.
Organization of the Temporary Military Airship Investigation Commission.
A conflagration at Osaka, 11,3[illegible]5 houses destroyed.
Korean Crown Prince starts on a tour through North-Eastern Japan with Prince Ito.

A big fire at Niigata. Promotion of Major-Generals I. Murata, F. Tanida, S. Iguchi, A. Saisho, K. Otani, S. Fujii, K. Akiyama & G. Nagaoka to Lieut.-Generals, and Colonels M. Kato, T. Kakizaki, K. Tachibana & S. Yokota to Major-Generals.
The Government announced to Chinese Government to proceed with the reconstruction of the Antung-Mukden Railway.
Training Squadron returned to Yokosuka.
The Tokyo Local Court's judgment on the sugar scandal M.P.'s. is confirmed at the Appeal Court.
Home Office issues regulations sternly forbidding all quasi-lottery affairs.
The Bank of Japan lowered the rate of interest.
Earthquake in Omi & Mino prefectures, 1,912 houses destroyed and 199 persons killed or wounded.
Businessmen going to America on invitation are honored by the Emperor with luncheon at the Shiba palace.
The Oriental Exploitation Co. established. Supplementary Agreement of the Kirin-Chang-chung Rly. loan signed. Count Futara dies.
The Japanese Businessmen start for America.
The Antung-Mukden Rly. convention signed.
Epxlosion of the Hirakata magazine near Osaka, destroying many houses.
The Emperor & Empress grant Yen 1,50[illegible] as relief to the sufferers by the late earthquake in Omi and Mino prefectures.
Korean Crown Prince returns to Tokyo.
The Airship Investigation Committee appointed.

a: Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Mineral Springs — [Most disastrous seismic calamities recorded in the pre-Tokugawa period]
t: Over 500,000 cho in southern part of Tosa subsided and engulfed by the sea.

a: Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Mineral Springs — [Most disastrous seismic calamities recorded in the pre-Tokugawa period]
t: Earthquakes with tidal waves visited Mutsu and thousands of people killed.

a: Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Mineral Springs — [Most disastrous seismic calamities recorded in the pre-Tokugawa period]
t: Earthquakes in districts. round about Kyoto.

a: Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Mineral Springs — [Most disastrous seismic calamities recorded in the pre-Tokugawa period]
t: Tokaido was visited by a severe earthquake, causing death of over 20,000 persons. Hamana Lagoon (Maizaka station, Tokaido Railway) formerly inland lake, was formed.

a: Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Mineral Springs — [Most disastrous seismic calamities recorded in the pre-Tokugawa period]
t: Bungo, Kyushu, was visited and 700 persons killed.

a: Earthquakes, Volcanoes and Mineral Springs — [Most disastrous seismic calamities recorded in the pre-Tokugawa period]
t: Districts round about Kyoto shaken and 2,000 persons killed.
Chinese books first introduced through Korea, 284 A.D.
Buddhism introduced from Korea, 552.
First authentic record of the sending to China for study of Japanese students, '607.
First school founded, 664.
First educational regulations promulgated, 701.
Oldest Japanese book extant, Kojiki, published, 712.
Printing introduced, 770.
Japanese alphabet invented by Buddhist priest Kobo, 809.
Revival of learning followed by the restoration of peace and the establishment of the Tokugawa Shogunate, 1602-1867.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 1. The Emperor's Oath on the occasion of his accession, that "public matters shall be decided by public assembly."

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 2. In 1873 Itagaki and others petitioned the Government to take steps for realizing the Imperial Oath.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 3. In 1880 a national organization for promoting the cause of popular rights was effected and in its name a petition was submitted to the Emperor for the immediate establishment of parliament.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 4. In 1880 the Provincial Assembly Regulations were enacted and popular craving was partially satisfied.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 5. In 1881 Itagaki and his fellow politicians organized the Liberal Party, and passed a resolution to push the movement with vigor.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 6. In the same year a proclamation was issued announcing the establishment of a national assembly ten years hence.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 7. In 1882 Okuma organized the Progressive Party.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 8. In 188[illegible] the Civil Corporation Regulations were enacted.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 9. On February 11th, 1889, the Constitution was promulgated.

a: Politics — Resume of the Growth of Constitutional Politics
t: 10. In November of the following year the first session of the Diet was convoked.
